reason: The text depicts the Egyptian Pharaoh and Egyptian authorities as antagonistic to the Hebrew people through forced labor and infanticide orders. The Hebrew leaders mentioned—specifically the midwives Shiphrah and Puah—are portrayed as protective of their people, deliberately disobeying the Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew male infants. Moses's parents are also shown as protective, hiding and preserving their son. No Hebrew leaders are portrayed as antagonistic to their own people in this passage.
